page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.32-64 is a compute instance based on the 64-bit Arm architecture. The system is equipped with 32 dedicated Ampere Altra physical cores running at a sustained clock speed of 3.0 GHz. Because the processor operates with a single thread per core and dedicated allocation, all 32 vCPUs map directly to independent physical execution pipelines, eliminating resource contention typical of simultaneous multithreading configurations.

System memory totals 64.0 GB, establishing an allocation ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local storage or hardware GPU accelerators, meaning persistent file systems require attached block storage volumes. One complimentary public IPv4 address is provided for external network connectivity.

With its 1:2 core-to-memory density, this configuration is oriented toward compute-focused parallel tasks rather than memory-heavy systems. The absence of hyperthreading provides deterministic performance characteristics across all processing units. The profile is functionally suited for multi-threaded code compilation, distributed microservices, batch processing pipelines, web serving, and data manipulation workloads compiled for arm64 execution environments.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.32-64 is a compute instance powered by the 64-bit Arm architecture. The configuration features 32 dedicated physical cores running on Ampere Altra processors at a fixed frequency of 3.0 GHz, yielding 32 single-threaded vCPUs with dedicated CPU allocation. Accompanying the compute capacity is 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 2.0 GB per-core allocation. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or GPU accelerators, necessitating remote block volumes for persistent data needs, while providing one complimentary public IPv4 address for network access. With an architectural focus on predictable core execution and a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio, the instance is structured for compute-heavy parallel operations. It offers strong qualitative resource efficiency for parallelized tasks, making it suited for multi-threaded software compilation, container fleets, web servers, data processing pipelines, and general scale-out Arm native workloads.
